# fs.exists callback and sync ownership

The original public fs.exists calls the legacy sync existsSync and invokes the callback immediately without validating it. The original existsSync stats the path directly and propagates invalid-path validation failures. Later genuine path-metadata installation supersedes access/mode/time methods but did not supersede either exists function. The generic legacy promise loop also synthesizes fs.promises.exists, which the pinned promise namespace does not export.

This slice selects the complete unchanged pinned lib/fs.js exists/custom-promisify/existsSync block (1316 bytes) through the existing pathMetadata public selection/generator. It consumes real initialized fs/process/Promise and util.promisify.custom identities. Existing Object.assign publication installs the actual selected functions; the one legacy promises-loop exclusion removes the invented promise namespace method. No new module, class, backend, flag or capability is introduced.

The pinned callback validates cb before path work, observes the actual VFS handler first, uses nextTick for a handled virtual path, and delegates to public fs.access with F_OK. That public indirection is intentional: the exact target uses it, including its synchronous throw suppression/callback(false) behavior. Ordinary real paths reach the existing access FSReqCallback, owned native MetadataWork, guest access syscall and actual callback scope; no synchronous stat is substituted as async completion. Custom util.promisify also follows public fs.exists using the captured intrinsic Promise, as the target does. There is no public fs.promises.exists export.

Sync existence uses the same exact pinned getValidatedPath/catch, DEP0187-once and VFS ordering. Its binding returns actual native fsMetadataSync('access', path, F_OK) status equality to0. This matches pinned node_file.cc ExistsSync on the guest POSIX path: actual uv_fs_access(...,0), errno means false. Native path snapshots and guest credentials/mount state remain authoritative. No native IO exception is swallowed outside the pinned validator catch; no fabricated filesystem metadata or fallback success. The Windows extra-stat branch is not a browser-host distinction: all Kandelo guests use their real shared POSIX syscall path.

The actual enabled Node Permission Model owner is still missing, including native ExistsSync's filesystem-read permission check. This slice does not fabricate permission admission or claim active permission-model support. VFS public installer/provider/loader activation, actual queue/GC/realm/OOM/fatal/Worker behavior and full fs namespace/descriptor/property shapes remain separate gaps. Current source code is not current guest execution, nor all-four-host conformance.
